title: Adaptive Phase-Feedforward Counter-Rotation vs. Non-Adaptive Quadrature Peeling
claims: At stage r of dyadic bit peeling with known prefix s_low = s mod 2^r, non-adaptive Pauli-X measurement has expectation (-1)^{b_r} gamma cos(phi_known) and suffers a complete blind spot at phi_known = +/- pi/2.
Adaptive counter-rotation R_Z(-phi_known) restores uniform Helstrom distinguishing bias D_TV = gamma across all 2^r prefixes s_low.
Adaptive phase-feedforward achieves an exact 2.0x Fisher-information / sample-complexity improvement over non-adaptive 50/50 random X/Y quadrature sampling.
favorable_controls: Stage r=1 mod 8 (blind spot at s_low=1 eliminated by R_Z(-pi/2))
Stage r=2 mod 16 with odd multiplier u=3
